preamble: Palatalization of the voiceless alveolar fricative [s] to [sʲ]: the tongue body is raised toward the hard palate during the consonant, typically before front vowels or a palatal glide. It is phonemic in Russian and Bulgarian and automatic before front vowels in Lithuanian. (In Irish the slender counterpart of broad /s/ is [ʃ], not [sʲ].)

examples.note: Proto-Slavic consonants before front vowels became palatalized in East Slavic; the palatalized series is now phonemic in Russian.
'to sit'; automatic palatalization before a front vowel
Stressed yat *ě became [ʲa] before a hard syllable in Eastern Bulgarian, leaving the preceding consonant palatalized.
